title: Муки совести Кости и улика Насти  (Kostya's Guilty Conscience and Nastya's Clue)

segments.t: After Chef Barinov chases Louis back to work with a poem, the female guest assumes Viktor Petrovich is Louis's jealous partner. Meanwhile, Kostya tells Sasha he can no longer hide their betrayal from Max, right before Nastya catches them arguing and notices Sasha's socks.
Да, это он.
И поэтому мне очень срочно нужно и бежать.
За дружбу?
Макс, вспомнил про Макс, у тебя совесть есть?
Я не знаю, как это все произойдет.
Пить надо меньше, как произошло.
Короче, я так больше не могу.
Я все расскажу Максу.
Что, опять случайность?
Саша, Макс должен знать правду.
Я все ему расскажу о нас.
Что тут делаешь?
Носки еще свои.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Да, это он.
'Yes, that is him.' Max favors a sharp approach in this beat, pairing "da" ("yes") with "eto" ("this") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.

За дружбу?
'To friendship?' Sasha prompts decisively to Kostya here, combining "druzhbu" ("friendship") and "za" ("for") so the key meaning lands right away.

'Max, speaking of Max, do you have a conscience at all?' Kostya prompts bluntly to Sasha here, leaning on "vspomnil" ("remembered") before closing the thought with "sovest" ("conscience").

'I do not know how all of this is going to play out.' Kostya brings a serious tempo during the exchange, pairing "znayu" ("know") with "kak" ("how") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Пить надо меньше, как произошло.

'You should have drunk less, that is how it happened.' Sasha conveys a natural approach in front of Max, building the phrase around "pit" ("drink") and "nado" ("it is necessary") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Короче, я так больше не могу.
'In short, I cannot take this anymore.' Max sets a lively direction on the spot, putting "koroche" ("long story short") alongside "bolshe" ("more") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Я все расскажу Максу.
'I am going to tell Max everything.' Kostya projects a calm course in their talk, joining "rasskazhu" ("will tell") to "ya" ("I") so every word pulls its weight.
Что, опять случайность?
'What, another coincidence?' Sasha challenges evenly in the scene, joining "opyat" ("again") to "sluchaynost" ("accident") so every word pulls its weight.
Саша, Макс должен знать правду.
'Sasha, Max deserves to know the truth.' Kostya picks an easygoing attitude toward Sasha, weaving "dolzhen" ("has to, must") together with "znat" ("to know") just the way native speakers do.

'I am going to tell him everything about us.' Kostya brings a steady mood without hesitation, leaning on "rasskazhu" ("will tell") before closing the thought with "ya" ("I").

'What are you doing in here?' Sasha wonders directly as the beat lands, combining "tut" ("here") and "delayesh" ("are you doing") so the key meaning lands right away.

'And wearing her socks, too.' Max favors a lively style without hesitation, leaning on "noski" ("socks") before closing the thought with "yeshche" ("still").
